These results provide evidence for incorporating snowmelt preconditioning into assessments of mountain vegetation risk that account for both event impacts and seasonal losses.

title: Empirical Reconstruction and a Pre-Specified GeoAI Evaluation Framework for Episodic Karst-Lake Drawdowns: Lake Jackson, Florida
summary: Episodic karst-lake drawdowns can outpace field observations. This Technical Note combines a satellite reconstruction of Lake Jackson, Florida, with a prespecified framework for evaluating future drawdown-anticipation models. We processed 333 Landsat 5 TM and Landsat 7 ETM+ Collection 2 Level-2 candidate scenes from 1984–2003; 167 observations passed coverage and quality screening. During the 1999–2001 drawdown, open-water area fell from a pre-event mean of 1061 ha to 64.9 ha on 3 July 2000, a loss of 93.9%. Comparison with in situ stage across 56 paired observations yielded an empirical stage–area relationship (R2 = 0.67; RMSE = 136 ha). Coverage-threshold sensitivity and precipitation-lag screening informed the subsequent evaluation design. That design specifies four lake-surface classes, objective event extraction, statistical and machine-learning baselines, spatially structured challengers, leave-one-drawdown-event-out validation, and a prespecified model-promotion rule. Predictive model comparisons and the planned groundwater, graph, precipitation, soil-moisture, and morphometric sensitivity tests have not been executed. The demonstrated contribution is a satellite reconstruction with an independent stage comparison; predictive skill remains to be evaluated.

title: Landslide Instance Segmentation from Remote Sensing Imagery Using a SwinV2–FPN Mask R-CNN with Spatially Adaptive Feature Modulation
summary: Landslide inventory mapping supports emergency response and hazard assessment in mountainous regions. Accurate identification and delineation of individual landslides remain challenging because of scale variation, irregular morphology, and interference from visually similar backgrounds in complex mountainous terrain. To address these challenges, we modified Mask R-CNN’s feature pathway and mask supervision. ResNet50 was replaced with SwinV2-Tiny for hierarchical feature extraction, while the feature pyramid network (FPN) was retained for multi-scale fusion. Spatially adaptive feature modulation (SAFM) was applied after the FPN to adjust spatial responses using local features and broader context. Binary cross-entropy (BCE) and Dice losses were combined to supervise pixel-wise foreground–background discrimination and instance-mask overlap. A curated dataset combining imagery from Bijie, the Diverse Mountainous Landslide Dataset (DMLD), and ScienceDB was used for training, validation, and internal testing. All configurations were evaluated using the Common Objects in Context (COCO) instance-mask protocol. Across three training seeds, SwinV2–FPN–SAFM Mask R-CNN achieved an internal test average precision (AP0.50:0.95) of 0.6158±0.0082 (mean ± sample standard deviation). Its mean mask AP0.50:0.95 exceeded those of ResNet50–FPN Mask R-CNN and Mask2Former–Swin-T by 6.21 and 3.51 percentage points, respectively. It achieved the highest mean mask AP0.50:0.95 among the ten evaluated configurations. The ablations indicated small positive increments in mean mask AP0.50:0.95 with SAFM and BCE–Dice, and their incremental benefits remained uncertain. The higher mean mask AP0.50:0.95 indicates improved overall performance in identifying landslide instances and delineating their extent on the internal test set. The resulting instance masks may assist inventory compilation and post-disaster mapping in complex mountainous terrain.

title: Long-Term Dynamics of Ulva prolifera Blooms in the Yellow Sea and Their Environmental Associations: Insights from Multi-Source Remote Sensing
summary: Recurrent Ulva prolifera (U. prolifera) green tides in the Yellow Sea have become a persistent coastal ecological problem, yet their long-term phenological changes and responses to environmental variability remain insufficiently understood. Here, we reconstructed the spatiotemporal dynamics of U. prolifera from 2008 to 2025 using multi-source satellite observations. Floating algae were detected using the Floating Algae Index (FAI) or Alternative Floating Algae Index (AFAI), and subpixel coverage was estimated using linear spectral unmixing. The results showed that MODIS-derived green tide extent expanded markedly, reaching 886.13 km2 in 2021. June exhibited the strongest long-term increasing trend. VIIRS observations showed broadly similar spatial and interannual bloom patterns over 2016–2025, while hourly GOCI-II observations revealed pronounced intraday variability which coverage generally increasing from morning to noon or afternoon. Environmental analyses demonstrated that bloom variability was jointly regulated by multiple environmental factors, including nonlinear relationships with sea surface temperature, pH, and dissolved oxygen, as well as linear effects of salinity and silicate. The multivariable model explained 70.7% of the observed variation in bloom area, highlighting the importance of coupled physical and biogeochemical controls. These findings indicate that Yellow Sea green tides are becoming increasingly persistent under changing environmental conditions. Multi-source satellite monitoring can inform adaptive management that combines nature-based solutions (NbS), including source-region nutrient reduction, optimized aquaculture structures, ecological polyculture with competitive macroalgae, hydrodynamic-based interception, and sustainable biomass utilization. Such approaches may reduce bloom risks while enhancing coastal ecosystem resilience and transforming U. prolifera management from passive removal toward proactive ecological regulation.

title: Coniferous Forest Change in the Great Salt Lake Basin 1986–2025: Snow Sublimation with Water-Resource Implications
summary: The Great Salt Lake in northern Utah, the USA, is at record-low levels, causing interest in factors that have reduced inflow. One potential factor is the expansion of coniferous forests, which intercept snow that sublimates to the atmosphere rather than reaching streams. We evaluated the increase in coniferous cover in the lake tributary basins and quantified the potential sublimation water loss. In Google Earth Engine we built annual summer–winter Landsat composites (14 features: six reflectance bands and NDVI for each season, 1986–2025) and classified coniferous forest using a 100-member Random Forest ensemble, giving an annual uncertainty envelope with a median run-to-run spread of 4.3%. We assessed trends with the Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope and estimated canopy sublimation as a fraction of snowfall. Coniferous cover in the Bear, Weber, and Jordan River tributary basins increased significantly over 1986–2025 (Sen’s slope +27 km2 yr−1, p = 0.00064; trend-based increase 1059 km2, about 35% of the 1986 extent). Applying Utah canopy-sublimation fractions (5–11% of snowfall) and a mean snowfall water equivalent of 0.71 m, the additional forest sublimates an estimated 30,000–67,000 acre-feet per year. While this is roughly 1.4–3.2% of mean annual river inflow, only a portion of the snowfall contributes to river flow, so the actual impact is lower, although loss is linear with snowfall.

title: ONOA-YOLO: Orthogonal-Nesting Orientation-Aware Small Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Object detection in remote sensing imagery is a fundamental and crucial task within the remote sensing domain. However, small object detection in remote sensing images remains a challenge for SOTA methods. This is because small objects often have large aspect ratios, exhibit characteristic variations across different orientations, and are distributed within complex backgrounds. Current methods, which employ square convolutions, often retain excessive background information during feature extraction, leading to suboptimal detection performance. In this paper, an orthogonal-nesting orientation-aware small object detection network based on YOLOv10 is proposed to achieve small object detection in complex backgrounds. ONOA-YOLO employs an orthogonal-nesting module to enhance the features of small objects from multiple orientations, improving the sensitivity of the network to their intrinsic features. Additionally, it incorporates a background-suppression module based on large convolutional kernels. This module integrates the contextual information of small objects as guiding cues with other features, enabling the suppression of background interference while preserving the extracted small object features.

title: Spatial Super-Resolution of Satellite-Derived SST Data via Generative Adversarial Networks in the Mediterranean Sea
summary: In this work, we compare deep convolutional and generative models to improve the reconstruction of sea surface temperature (SST) gradients and effective resolution from cloud-contaminated satellite infrared data. Standard gap-filling techniques produce spatially complete datasets, but they inherently smooth out fine-scale features and gradients that may be critical for a better understanding of the ocean dynamics. Here, we investigate how the use of deep learning models as Autoencoders (AEs) and generative models as Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (C-GANs) differently contribute to recovering the small-scale structures lost during interpolation. Our supervised, observation-based training relies on satellite-derived SST data from the Mediterranean Sea, with a focus on learning the statistical relationship between high-resolution fields and their low-resolution counterparts. We apply a tiling and merging strategy to deal with limited observational coverage and to ensure spatial continuity. Quantitative validation based on mean squared error metrics, spectral analysis, and gradient statistics shows that the AE reduces the reconstruction error, but it fails to recover high-frequency variability. In contrast, the C-GAN effectively restores the statistical properties of the true SST field at the cost of increasing the pointwise discrepancy with the ground truth observations. Our results highlight the potential of deep models to enhance the physical and statistical realism of gap-filled satellite data in oceanographic applications.

title: Radial Spectral Barcode Watermarking for Remote Sensing Images: Extending the Detectable Scale Limits
summary: To extend the scale limits within which a template watermark remains detectable, this paper proposes a template watermarking algorithm for remote sensing images based on a radial spectral barcode (RSB). The RSB is a new geometry of template watermark whose inner and outer boundaries are separated along the radial direction of the discrete Fourier transform magnitude spectrum. In the embedding stage, the spectrum is divided into angular slots, a synchronization sequence generated from the secret key and the watermark are assigned to alternate slots, and the magnitude within the radial interval of each slot is modulated according to its sign. In the detection stage, the angular profile of the received spectrum is computed under a set of geometric hypotheses, the synchronization sequence is located by circular correlation, and the watermark is read from the synchronized profile without correcting the image. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method extends the detectable scale interval well beyond that of the ring-template methods while retaining robustness against rotation, translation, cropping, affine transformation, map reprojection, and signal-processing attacks. It outperforms the comparative algorithms in robustness at an equal or higher PSNR, with a low false detection rate.

title: FLNet: A Deep Learning Detector for Floating-Debris Detection in Close-Range Aquatic Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Floating debris threatens aquatic ecosystems, yet detecting it in close-range aquatic remote sensing imagery remains difficult because small, irregular, or partially submerged objects resemble specular highlights and ripples. This study proposes FLNet, a YOLO11-L-based detector for water-surface monitoring from unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). FLNet redesigns the backbone, neck, and head with three components: a Dynamic Polarity-Aware Robustness Block that calibrates deep activations and models similar and opposing feature relations; an Adaptive Multi-Receptive Pyramid that repeatedly fuses three adjacent scales through multi-branch depthwise convolutions; and a Detail-Preserving Shared Head that applies one boundary-sensitive prediction trunk to all scales. On a custom five-category dataset of 12,237 images, FLNet achieved 85.93% macro-Precision, 85.08% macro-F1, and 88.77% mean average Precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.5 (mAP@0.5), the highest single-run values among the evaluated detectors, with 24M parameters and 83 GFLOPs. Across three random seeds, its macro-Precision and macro-F1 advantages over the strongest competitor, Hyper-YOLO, exceeded seed-to-seed variability, whereas its mAP@0.5 was statistically comparable to that of Hyper-YOLO and Hyper-YOLO retained a higher mAP@0.5:0.95. In separately trained benchmarks, FLNet achieved the highest F1-score on FloW-Img (80.26%) and the highest macro-F1 on MarineDebris-yolo (79.82%). With TensorRT half-precision (FP16) acceleration, detector-side inference reached 29.8, 111.2, and 56.4 frames per second on Jetson Xavier NX, AGX Orin, and Orin Nano Super, respectively. FLNet therefore offers a favorable accuracy–efficiency balance for close-range floating-debris detection.

title: Review on the Precise Microwave Brightness Temperature Transfer in the Radiometer Calibration Link
summary: The transfer of precise reference brightness temperature (BT) from the microwave calibration target (MCT) to the receiver antenna is a significant and fundamental issue in achieving accurate microwave radiometer calibration. In addition to the issues of receiver nonlinearity, gain stability et al., this review focuses on the electromagnetic field propagation process. Addressing the precise brightness temperature transfer from the MCT to the receiving antenna in the near-field region, this review systematically summarizes recent research progress by domestic and international scholars on the electromagnetic and thermal emission characteristics of MCT, as well as brightness temperature transfer modeling methodologies and their intrinsic properties. Or in other words, from the perspectives of (1) the accurate BT emission from the MCT, and (2) the accurate transferring in the calibration link, as they are the physical foundation of the radiometer calibration process and corresponding problems took decades to be tackled. This review aims to provide a comprehensive reference encompassing theories, methodologies, and fundamental mechanisms for the progressive establishment of microwave brightness temperature standards and transfer standards by discussing specific issues regarding how MCTs can be accurately characterized and how the BT can be precisely transferred.

title: Lightweight Dual-Branch Target-Aware Network for Land-Based Hyperspectral Camouflage Target Detection
summary: Hyperspectral camouflaged target detection is challenging because target and background spectra are highly coupled, positive pixels are extremely scarce, and scene-dependent spectral variation limits cross-dataset robustness. Existing detectors often rely on a single spectral representation or use spatial models with substantial parameters and computation, which may discard complementary evidence or increase deployment costs. This article presents a lightweight dual-branch target-aware network for land-based hyperspectral camouflage target detection. The model preserves fine raw spectral details and whitened PCA features while integrating multi-scale spatial context. A target-aware spatial gate is further employed to suppress background-like responses, and a center-aware decision head alleviates the dilution of small targets during patch pooling. Class-weighted loss and balanced sampling address severe class imbalance. On four land-based hyperspectral camouflage datasets with 1% training, 4% validation, and 95% testing pixels, the proposed method achieves F1 scores of 0.9438–0.9601, PR-AUC values of 0.9814–0.9938, and false-alarm rates of 0.0002–0.0003, outperforming eight representative detectors. Ablation studies confirm the complementarity of the raw and PCA branches and the effectiveness of the target-aware gate and center-aware head. In cross-dataset evaluation with only 0.5% target pixels for fine-tuning and another 0.5% for validation, PR-AUC remains between 0.8833 and 0.9288. The model requires only 0.0556 M parameters and 8.0699 M FLOPs per patch, indicating a favorable trade-off between accuracy, generalization, and lightweight deployment.

title: Estimation of Cut and Fill and Removed Tree Volume for Forest Road Design Using Fused Aerial and Terrestrial Laser Scans: A Case Study from Oregon, USA
summary: Efficient planning of forest roads is essential to sustaining uninterrupted forestry activities and supporting sustainable forest management. Roads must be designed in concert with existing infrastructure while conforming to operational requirements for timber extraction, accessibility, and environmental compliance. Advances in high-resolution remote sensing and computational geomatics enable acquisition of high-precision, three-dimensional descriptions of forest structure integrable into geographic information systems (GISs) for route optimization and terrain modeling. Despite this progress, a formal procedure for designing forest roads from point clouds derived by combining aerial and terrestrial laser scanning is not yet established. This study addresses that gap by presenting a complete, reproducible workflow for forest road design using fused airborne and near-ground laser scanning point clouds. The workflow encompasses three stages: LiDAR acquisition and derivation of topographic and vegetation attributes, optimal route identification, and estimation of standing timber volume within the proposed corridor. The procedure is demonstrated on a 200 m test section within the McDonald-Dunn Research Forest of Oregon State University, where 133 trees were inventoried and cut and fill volumes quantified. The results confirm that LiDAR-based planning achieves sub-0.12 m accuracy while enabling precise quantification of standing stock to be removed, reducing field time, improving cost efficiency, and supporting data-driven environmental decision-making.

title: OptiX-Based SAR Image Simulation with Residual-Learning Refinement
summary: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery plays an important role in disaster monitoring, environmental monitoring, and related applications. However, the acquisition of measured SAR data is limited by high costs and the difficulty of covering diverse environmental conditions, and the volume of SAR imagery is far smaller than that of optical remote sensing imagery, which restricts learning-based SAR applications. This paper proposes a multi-view SAR image simulation method based on OptiX and residual learning. The proposed method uses the NVIDIA OptiX ray-tracing API to simulate electromagnetic wave propagation, uses Monte Carlo sampling to model material interactions and coherent summation to form SAR images, and generates multi-view SAR image sequences of buildings. The simulator uses a scalar multiple-bounce approximation, and simulation, refinement, and evaluation use only the HH channel. The OptiX-based simulator is coupled with a residual U-Net that predicts the residual between simulated and measured images and compensates for missing fine-scale details. The method supports efficient multi-view generation. Quantitative validation on the SARMV3D dataset shows that the refined simulated images achieve low pixel-level error and high structural and perceptual similarity, yielding average values of 23.88 dB for the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), 0.83 for the structural similarity index measure (SSIM), and 0.20 for learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS). The method provides an effective means for generating multi-view SAR images of buildings, has potential for use in downstream tasks such as target recognition, is physically interpretable, and shows promising generalization capability across the evaluated building scenes.

title: Residual Viewing-Geometry Dependence in Provisional NISAR L-Band GCOV Backscatter over a Steep Mediterranean Pine Forest
summary: Radiometric terrain correction normalises an illuminated-area contribution to NISAR GCOV backscatter, but intrinsic angular scattering can remain. We evaluated terrain-associated variation in seven provisional granules acquired during June–July 2026 over Paphos Forest, Cyprus, using 422,996 stable Pinus brutia cells on a 20 m analysis grid and an independent 1 m ALS terrain survey. Generalised additive mixed models were assessed with buffered spatial cross-validation and a spatial cluster bootstrap. With the supplied-look log-bias adjustment, conditional-path spans are approximately 1.3 dB in HH and 2.2 dB in HV; alternative ENL multipliers yield 1.280–1.785 dB and 1.598–2.228 dB, respectively. Ascending-minus-descending differences reverse sign with viewing geometry, and the pattern recurs in three acquisition pairs despite a change in the sign of their humidity contrast. Operational-DEM geometry predicts the paired difference better than the tested ALS geometry, although sub-pixel registration narrows the gap. DEM-disagreement and polarisation-specific geometry terms retain small predictive gains across alternative spatial partitions. These results describe associations at one site and product version. They do not separate intrinsic scattering, normalisation error, and acquisition effects; orbit direction, track, and overpass time remain confounded.

title: Vision Transformer-Based Conditional Modeling for Forest Stratified Canopy Height Estimation
summary: Accurate estimation of stratified forest canopy height is crucial for understanding forest dynamics and estimating carbon stocks. While remote sensing is widely used for regional canopy mapping, its accuracy is often limited in mountainous and dense forests, particularly for understory canopy layers, because of signal saturation and restricted sensor penetration through the overstory canopy. To address these issues, we design a novel deep learning model, which combines the self-attention mechanism and the Vision Transformer encoder–decoder architecture (ViT-ed) with conditional modeling to achieve precise prediction of stratified canopy height using multi-temporal Sentinel-1/2 and Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) data. This model structure is tailored to the ecological correlations between vertical forest layers and optimized with a hybrid loss function and achieves significant improvements over the encoder-only convolutional neural network baseline (CNN-e). Validated against field inventory data, our model achieves a correlation coefficient of 0.843 (root mean square error (RMSE) = 1.532 m) for overstory canopy height and 0.825 (RMSE = 0.377 m) for understory canopy height, markedly outperforming the CNN-e benchmarks (RMSE = 1.846 m and 0.451 m, respectively). These results demonstrate improved understory canopy height estimation relative to CNN-e in the study area. Based on freely available data, this method generates continuous canopy height maps for the study area and has potential to enhance carbon stock estimation across broader regions.

title: Ultra-Long-Term InSAR Deformation Assessment Through Statistical Harmonization of Multi-Release EGMS Data and Hydro-Deformation Regime Concordance Analysis
summary: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) products from the European Ground Motion Service (EGMS) are released through successive, partially overlapping temporal windows, offering the potential to construct ultra-long-term (ULT) deformation records, i.e., continuous records spanning multiple releases and exceeding the 5–6-year extent of any individual release. However, direct combination of independently processed releases may introduce artificial offsets and trend changes. This study presents an enhanced Temporal Alignment via Statistical Testing (TAST) procedure to harmonize four EGMS Ortho releases (R1–R4; January 2016–December 2024) over the Lecco–Como area of northern Italy in both Up–Down and East–West components. The method applies translation and linear velocity correction optimized through a joint Cramér–von Mises/RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) objective while preserving within-release deformation evolution. The resulting ULT records were segmented at three regional groundwater-level (GWL) turning points (TPs) and analyzed using the introduced Hydro-Deformation Regime Concordance (HDRC) metric. The results show that inter-release velocity discrepancies reached 7.12 mm/y in U-D and 11.21 mm/y in E-W, demonstrating their potential to substantially alter apparent long-term deformation regimes. Vertical deformation was predominantly anti-concordant with GWL turning behavior, with 59.7–69.9% negative HDRC, whereas E-W responses evolved from strong positive HDRC dominance to near-balanced conditions. HDRC exhibited significant spatial organization (Moran’s I up to 0.51) and geological association (Cramér’s up to 0.31), while geological-group response rankings remained persistent across successive hydro-regime transitions (Kendall’s W up to 0.88). A screening of potential alternative regional drivers identified no clear evidence that seismicity, capable faults, or isolated extreme precipitation events accounted for the observed multi-TP patterns. These results demonstrate that systematic multi-release EGMS harmonization enables temporally consistent long-term monitoring and reveals non-stationary, spatially structured, and geologically conditioned deformation responses associated with groundwater dynamics.

title: Beyond a Single Look Azimuth: A Composite Approach to Directional Wave Spectra Retrieval from Coastal X-Band Radar
summary: Remote sensing systems, and X-band marine radar (MR) specifically, enable the acquisition of directional wave spectra (DWS) over a wide spatial coverage by processing backscatter images. It has been shown that the MR look azimuth has a significant impact on the accuracy of the resulting DWS. While the effect of azimuthal dependency is observed in both deep and shallow water, it becomes critical for measurements in coastal environments, where spectral properties change frequently due to wave refraction, reflection, and dissipation. In this study, shore-based MR data are used to process DWS and integrated wave parameters across different wave regimes. The dependence of the DWS uncertainties on the look azimuth is evaluated via comparison with concurrent Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP) measurements. We propose a retrieval strategy that composites multiple sub-images sampled at different look azimuths along a common isobath, so that every window captures the same stage of wave shoaling, for a more accurate evaluation of DWS and integrated wave parameters. The approach assumes an alongshore-uniform bathymetry, a condition met at the present site and common to gently sloping sandy coasts, and its applicability to irregular shorelines is considered in the discussion. The developed composite approach enhances the ability of the MR to accurately resolve sea-state directionality even in the case of multiple interacting wave systems. Cross-validation against the ADCP shows that the retrieved mean wave direction can differ by up to 30 between extreme look azimuths, and that the composite scheme recovers directionality with the best-balanced error metrics across the tested methods. These results argue against reliance on any single MR window for coastal directional monitoring. This advancement is essential for coastal engineering applications, as even directional misinterpretations of a few degrees can significantly alter the estimates of longshore sediment transport.

title: MambaDPSMVS: Remote Sensing Multi-View Height Estimation Based on Mamba-Enhanced Feature Pyramid and Deformable RPC Sampler
summary: Aiming at the problems of complex RPC geometric modeling in multi-view stereo matching (MVS) of satellite remote-sensing images, significant feature noise caused by cross-view occlusion and inconsistent lighting, and blurred edge details of height maps, this paper proposes a satellite MVS height estimation network based on a Mamba-enhanced feature pyramid and deformable RPC sampling, MambaDPSMVS. In the feature extraction stage, the cross-view Mamba module and the single-view self-Mamba enhancement module are designed to realize explicit feature interaction between and within views through direction prediction, direction routing, geometric gating fusion and state-space sequence modeling, and suppress view noise from the source. A deformable sampler for an RPC geometry, RPC-DPSampler, is proposed to achieve accurate alignment of source-view features with the reference view through 3D deformable coarse alignment, block sampling, 2D sub-pixel fine-tuning and view-level attention-weighted aggregation. Then, the cascaded cost is constructed, and the loop encoder–decoder regularization is used to complete the height estimation from coarse to fine. Experiments on the WHU-TLC and US3D datasets show that the MAE/RMSE of the proposed method reaches 1.688 m/2.867 m and 1.744 m/3.847 m, respectively, and the PAG<1 m reaches 61.81% and 62.18%, respectively, which values are better than those of baseline methods such as Sat (Red-Net) and Sat (CasMVS-Net). The ablation experiment further validated the complementarity of Mamba enhancement features and the RPC-DPSampler module in feature expression and geometric alignment.

title: Mitigating Spatiotemporal Error Clustering in SIF Downscaling: A Novel Zoning Strategy Achieves High-Accuracy Reconstruction
summary: Spatiotemporally refined solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) information over large regions has become a crucial data source for terrestrial carbon cycle studies and agricultural drought stress monitoring. Various machine learning (ML) methods have been employed to reconstruct satellite-based SIF retrievals, addressing issues such as spatial gaps and coarse resolution. However, the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in the statistical relationships between explanatory variables and SIF introduces potential errors in these empirical models, leading to spatiotemporal error aggregation. This study proposes a novel spatiotemporal zoning strategy to reconstruct GOME-2 SIF. The Spatiotemporal Ensemble (STE) model integrates multi-source geospatial data and diverse ML models, demonstrating superior SIF estimation performance. The STE model achieved an R2 of 0.925 with 5-fold cross-validation and an RMSE of 0.058 mW m−2 sr−1 nm−1, outperforming six classical ML models by 14%. The STE model significantly mitigates spatiotemporal error aggregation. Temporally, the seasonal variability in model performance was reduced, with the RMSE gap between months with peak and trough errors decreasing to merely 0.04 mW m−2 sr−1 nm−1. Spatially, error clustering trends were weakened. We successfully generated a reconstructed SIF product for China at 0.01°/8-day spatiotemporal resolution spanning 2008 to 2018. Reducing spatiotemporal error aggregation in SIF estimation will enhance its application potential.

title: Wind Speed Retrieval for CDWL via Multi-Range Gate with Sup-Adap Frequency Estimation and CNN-LSBoost Model
summary: Multi-range-gate wind retrieval with coherent Doppler wind LiDAR (CDWL) remains challenging under a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and precipitation: low SNR, spectral-edge peaks and system gain drift destabilize the radial frequency estimation, and multi-beam synthesis further amplifies the errors, directly affecting the reliability of vertical wind profiles. This study develops a multi-range-gate wind retrieval framework that couples physical constraints with data-driven regression. After spectral accumulation and quality control (QC), an adaptive super-noise centroid (sup-adap) estimator extracts radial velocities, and a CNN-LSBoost model maps the multi-beam radial velocities of adjacent range gates to the horizontal wind. The framework was evaluated with prescribed winds in simulations and validated against independent meteorological-tower observations from a field experiment under moderate rain, with training and test hours strictly separated. Against the tower, CNN-LSBoost achieved R² = 0.983, RMSE = 0.42 m/s and P95 = 0.53 m/s, outperforming KNN+GA, RF+GWO, CNN and Transformer baselines. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides a validated route to reliable wind profiling under low-SNR and precipitation conditions.

title: Remote-Sensing-Supported Transboundary Ecosystem Service Mapping: A Robust Integrated Index for the Heilongjiang–Amur River Basin
summary: Comparable ecosystem service mapping across international borders requires inputs and choices that remain consistent across the study area. We harmonized satellite-derived and geospatial datasets for the Heilongjiang–Amur River Basin to a common 1 km grid for 2000, 2010, and 2020. Landsat-derived land cover, MODIS burned area, harmonized nighttime lights, terrain, climate, and modeled soil products supported four InVEST indicators: Habitat Quality, Carbon Storage, Annual Water Yield, and Soil Retention. Pooled p01–p99 normalization and equal weighting produced a dimensionless, relative, modeled integrated ES index. Robustness was assessed using alternative normalization, leave-one-service-out tests, bounded weight perturbation, land-cover-excluded XGBoost–SHAP models, and spatially blocked cross-validation. The basin-wide mean index values were 0.444, 0.461, and 0.451. The Chinese-side means were 0.357, 0.365, and 0.361, compared to 0.528, 0.555, and 0.538 on the Russian side; the Russia–China contrast remained positive across tested construction alternatives. The random-split R2 values were 0.819, 0.806, and 0.793, whereas the spatially blocked R2 values were 0.651, 0.582, and 0.606. SHAP analysis characterized associations in fitted predictions rather than causal effects. The three benchmark-year differences are indicative and remain sensitive to Annual Water Yield, interannual climate, and index construction.

title: Tracking Earth’s Energy Imbalance: CERES Radiative Analysis, Heat Uptake Comparisons, and Perspectives from the Uvsq-Sat Nano-Satellite Series
summary: Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI) is the small residual between absorbed solar radiation and outgoing thermal radiation at the top of the atmosphere (TOA). We analyse global monthly fluxes from the Clouds and the Earth’s Radiant Energy System (CERES) Energy Balanced and Filled (EBAF) Ed4.2.1 record from March 2000 to March 2026, together with complementary solar, cloud, greenhouse gas, El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), sea surface temperature (SST), sea-ice, and ocean heat content datasets. Over 2001–2025, the CERES net TOA radiative flux (NET) anomaly relative to 2001–2020 shows a trend of +0.451±0.196Wm−2decade−1 (95% confidence interval; R2=0.496). The algebraic decomposition of this trend using N=ISR−OSR−OLR, where ISR, OSR, and OLR denote incoming solar radiation, reflected shortwave radiation, and outgoing longwave radiation, respectively, yields component contributions of +0.071, +0.806, and −0.426Wm−2decade−1. The reduction in reflected shortwave radiation is therefore the largest positive contribution to the observed NET trend. Raw annual correlations with greenhouse gas indicators, SST, and sea ice are substantially weakened after detrending. When accounting for annual serial correlation and false discovery rate (FDR) control, only CERES cloud area and ocean heat uptake from the Estimating the Circulation and Climate of the Ocean (ECCO) state estimate retain significant annual associations with NET. Detrended monthly lag analyses further show significant negative relationships between CERES NET and the Niño-3.4 and MEI.v2 indices, with the strongest correlations occurring when the ENSO indices precede NET by approximately 6–7 months. Over the strictly common 222-month interval (July 2005–December 2023), CERES NET shows strong temporal covariability with complementary heat-uptake estimates. The correlation coefficients over this common interval are r=0.857 for ECCO ocean heat uptake and r=0.804 for the planetary heat-storage estimate including atmospheric energy tendency. The corresponding detrended correlations are r=0.760 and r=0.640, respectively. The Uvsq-Sat NET record overlaps CERES observations, while Uvsq-Sat NG continues this measurement sequence. Its current time series remains too short to support climatological or long-term trend analyses and is therefore not yet used for such analyses. These results motivate a hybrid observing architecture combining reference radiometers, cross-calibrated broadband nano-satellites, targeted spectral measurements, and planetary heat-storage estimates.

title: Activity and Rainfall Response of the Gimigliano Landslide (Southern Italy): Insights from SBAS-InSAR Data Analysis
summary: Slow-moving landslides are complex systems characterized by marked spatial and temporal variability in deformation, which may be difficult to capture using landslide-wide displacement measures. This study investigates the Gimigliano landslide (Calabria, southern Italy), a large, long-lived and urbanized slope instability, by integrating multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SBAS-InSAR observations, data-driven kinematic segmentation, geomorphological analysis and rainfall–deformation relationships. InSAR time series were clustered to identify spatially coherent kinematic domains, which were subsequently compared with independently mapped geomorphological sectors. Continuous and event-based analyses were then used to investigate the temporal relationship between rainfall and landslide deformation. Four kinematic domains were identified, with the highest domain-averaged deformation rates reaching approximately −12.8 mm/yr in the vertical component and −4.8 mm/yr in the east–west component. The identified domains show a clear spatial correspondence with the geomorphological elements of the landslide. Rainfall–deformation relationships showed the highest-magnitude correlations for 60–120 days rainfall accumulation windows, with maximum correlations occurring at lags of approximately 30–35 days for the vertical component and 60–75 days for the east–west component. Event-based analysis further highlighted variable response magnitudes among domains and delayed responses within a few weeks. The results indicate that deformation is associated with antecedent hydrological conditions while retaining substantial spatial heterogeneity, highlighting the value of integrating InSAR, geomorphological and rainfall information for the interpretation of slow-moving landslide dynamics.

title: A Downscaling–Calibration Framework for GPM Precipitation Data Based on Geographically Weighted Machine Learning: A Case Study of the Yellow River Basin, China
summary: Satellite precipitation products alleviate sparse gauge coverage, but their coarse resolution limits hydrometeorological applications. This study develops and evaluates an integrated downscaling–calibration framework for the Yellow River Basin, China, using Geographical-XGBoost (G-XGBoost) for downscaling and Geographical Difference Analysis (GDA) for calibration. Geographically weighted regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost were used for comparison. Fraction disaggregation was compared with an optimal-lag Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) method for monthly disaggregation. Using Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) data and four explanatory variables, including NDVI, Land Surface Temperature (LST), Digital Elevation Model (DEM), and slope, the spatial resolution was improved from 0.1° to 1 km. The downscaled products covered both annual and monthly temporal resolutions. Results show that: (1) G-XGBoost achieved relatively strong overall performance among the four downscaling models before GDA correction across the dry year 2015, wet year 2018, and near-average year 2019, while after GDA correction, all products improved and G-XGBoost remained among the best-performing methods across the three years; and (2) at the monthly scale, fraction disaggregation showed modest numerical improvements in pooled accuracy across the three-year comparison, although its relative performance varied among years and metrics. The framework provides a practical approach for generating high-spatial-resolution precipitation estimates in the Yellow River Basin.

title: Deep Learning-Based Mapping of Floating Kelp Forests from Sentinel-2 Imagery
summary: Kelp forests are vital marine habitats with significant ecological, cultural, and economic importance. These ecosystems, found along coastlines, are susceptible to regional and global stressors including coastal development and climate change. This paper presents Satellite-based Kelp Mapping (SKeMa), a novel framework for automatically mapping canopy-forming kelp forests along the coast of British Columbia using Sentinel-2 satellite scenes. SKeMa employs a deep learning semantic segmentation model, offering an efficient alternative to traditional, labor-intensive, and time-consuming kelp-mapping methods. Here, we initially evaluated SKeMa against two conventional, non-deep-learning baselines, NDVI thresholding and Random Forest, and several alternative deep learning architectures. For the best-performing model, an ablation study on input channels identifies a suitable input configuration, and a cross-validation study with independent test sets yields a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.6024 and F1-score of 0.7491. Average precision and recall are 0.7261 and 0.7951, respectively. Overall, the highest validation metrics were for images with medium to large kelp beds and the lowest for images with small kelp beds, likely because Sentinel-2’s spatial resolution limits mapping of small kelp beds. These results are achieved under a highly imbalanced class distribution, with labeled kelp pixels constituting, on average, less than 0.1% of all pixels in a Sentinel-2 scene. The results demonstrate the model’s ability to detect kelp canopies across diverse coastal regions, particularly for medium to large kelp beds.

title: Multi-Granularity Text and Scale-Aware Visual Encoding for Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval and Prompt-Based Scene Recognition
summary: Remote sensing captions typically interleave domain-specific terminology, object attributes, spatial relations, and scene context within a single sentence, while the corresponding imagery contains targets spanning markedly different spatial extents—from individual vehicles to entire airport layouts. A single global text vector and fixed-scale visual pooling therefore tend to discard the local and hierarchical evidence needed for reliable image–text alignment. Moreover, standard contrastive objectives treat all unmatched pairs as equally unrelated, ignoring the fact that semantically adjacent scenes (e.g., airports and industrial zones) share substantial visual content. To address these issues, we develop a CLIP-style dual encoder with three targeted additions: a text encoder that preserves word-level, phrase-level, and sentence-level representations before fusing them through cross-granularity attention; a visual encoder that associates four hierarchical feature levels with scale-aware receptive-field configurations and incorporates SAM-guided local views during training; and a semantic membership-aware contrastive loss that applies detached, bounded discount weights to semantically close negatives without inverting their penalty sign. On the cleaned RSICD benchmark, the model achieves 87.5% mAP for in-domain prompt-based scene recognition and 34.37% mean recall for scene-constrained retrieval, outperforming the quoted RemoteCLIP and fully fine-tuned CLIP results in the scene-constrained retrieval comparison. Ablation confirms that each of the three components contributes meaningfully to the final performance. The deployable dual encoder contains approximately 59.7 million trainable parameters, and SAM is not required at inference.

title: Monitoring Lakes in Mountains with Sentinel-1 SAR Imagery
summary: Lakes are crucial markers of climate fluctuations, yet identifying water bodies in mountainous regions remains a persistent challenge for satellite remote sensing due to terrain-induced obstacles and dynamic surface conditions of ice and snow. We present a novel approach based solely on Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data that allows for the detection of lakes as well as the tracking of their surface area and conditions in mountainous terrain. Our methodology is built around a new index called OASIS, which uses pairs of SAR images to detect and monitor lake surface conditions. We show that this index provides critical insights into lake surface conditions, including the onset and duration of ice cover and the observation of frozen lakes concealed beneath snow. We evaluate this capacity using in situ lake temperature measurements at Arpont Lake. At this lake, the estimated open-water onset typically occurs in mid- to late July, with an ice-free season lasting roughly three to three and a half months. The years 2017 and especially 2022 stand out, showing an earlier break-up (2 July and 24 June, respectively) and longer open-water periods (114 and 132 days; revisit 6 days in 2017–2021 and 12 days in 2016 and 2022–2024). When combined with a segmentation technique, the index allows for accurate quantification and tracking of temporal changes in lake surface area, highlighting lakes that experienced severe drought from 2016 to 2024 in the French Alps. We successfully validated our lake surface area estimates using state-of-the-art lake databases derived from optical sensors.

title: Glacier Volume Changes Across the Greater Caucasus Between 1960 and 2025
summary: Mountain glaciers are sensitive indicators of climate change and provide essential freshwater resources for downstream ecosystems and human societies. Although glacier area changes have been extensively investigated in the Greater Caucasus, no long-term assessments of regional glacier ice volume reconstruction have been made. This study presents the first comprehensive reconstruction of glacier ice volume changes across the entire Greater Caucasus over the past 65 years, integrating glacier inventories at five observational periods (1960, 1986, 2000, 2014, and 2025) with the automated PalaeoIce reconstruction framework. Total glacier ice volume declined from 88.08 ± 4.5 km3 in 1960 to 42.66 ± 1.1 km3 in 2025, corresponding to an overall loss of more than half of the Caucasus glacier volume (51.6%) since 1960. Ice volume loss accelerated markedly after 2000, with the most rapid decline (27% or −2.45 yr−1) occurring between 2014 and 2025. Spatial patterns in ice volume change show pronounced regional variability. Relative ice loss over the past 65 years was greatest among glaciers in Azerbaijan, which experienced a 98.4% reduction in ice volume. In comparison, glaciers in Georgia and Russia lost 52.6% and 50.9% of their ice volume, respectively, over the same period. Sectoral analysis further reveals contrasting spatial responses across the Greater Caucasus, with the eastern sector experiencing the greatest proportional ice loss of 71.6% over the 65-year study period, followed by the western sector with 60.4% and the central sector with 47.3%. Despite the continuous regional decline in total ice volume, mean reconstructed glacier thickness increased from ~28.2 m in 1960 to ~33.5 m in 2000 before declining to ~17.4 m by 2025 for the entire Greater Caucasus, indicating substantial changes in the regional glacier-size distribution and geometry through time. These findings provide region-wide quantification of long-term glacier ice volume and thickness evolution in the Greater Caucasus and establish an important baseline for assessing glacier response to ongoing climate change, future water availability, natural hazards, and regional cryospheric evolution.

title: Deep Learning-Based Detection and Severity Classification of Individual Trees Damaged by Dendrolimus sibiricus Using UAV Multispectral Imagery and LiDAR Data
summary: Outbreaks of the Siberian silk moth (Dendrolimus sibiricus) pose an increasingly serious threat to larch forests in Mongolia, particularly as rising air temperatures and increasing drought frequency create favorable conditions for pest proliferation, degrading forest ecosystem stability. This study presents a UAV-based deep learning (DL) framework that integrates multispectral (MS) and LiDAR sensor data to detect individual trees and classify their health condition in a Dendrolimus sibiricus-affected larch forest. Field surveys were conducted over a 59-hectare study area using UAV flights during the pre-pesticide application period. Vegetation indices (NDVI, GNDVI, NDRE and CIRE) combined with tree structural point cloud data were employed to train a Mask R-CNN DL model to classify tree health into 3 classes: (i) healthy, (ii) moderate and (iii) severely damaged. The model was evaluated on 10 held-out test plots, containing 573 trees. Detection precision, recall and F1-score were 0.679, 0.684 and 0.682, while Total (detection plus correct health class) precision, recall and F1-score were 0.627, 0.632 and 0.630, respectively. Compared with spectral-only input (RGB plus vegetation indices), the full 10-channel input improved the Detection F1 from 0.675 to 0.682 and the Total F1 from 0.619 to 0.630. The findings contribute to forest pest early warning systems, hotspot identification and forest health monitoring in Mongolia.

title: Airborne Hyperspectral LWIR Emissivity Data for Urban Surface-Material Characterisation: A Case Study in Dessau, Germany
summary: Urban environments consist of highly heterogeneous surface materials whose physical and radiative properties influence surface energy exchange, heat storage, and urban microclimate conditions. While urban materials have been extensively investigated in the visible, near-infrared, and shortwave-infrared regions, their characterisation in the long-wave infrared (LWIR) domain remains comparatively limited, particularly using airborne hyperspectral imaging. This study assesses the potential of airborne hyperspectral LWIR emissivity data for urban surface-material characterisation and discrimination. Hyperspectral data were acquired over Dessau-Roßlau, Germany, using the Telops Hyper-Cam Airborne Mini. The radiance data were geometrically corrected, mosaicked, atmospherically compensated, and processed using temperature-emissivity separation to derive a 66-band emissivity mosaic. After MNF-based denoising, 11 material endmembers were extracted from a representative urban-industrial subset, including asphalt, concrete, cobblestone, bitumen roofing, metal surfaces, solar panels, storage silos, tree cover, and sparse grass. Selected airborne endmembers showed generally consistent spectral shapes when compared with independent ECOSTRESS and LUMA laboratory reference spectra. Linear and radial basis function Support Vector Machine classifications were then applied and evaluated using spatially independent validation regions. The linear SVM achieved the highest overall accuracy of 84.95%, balanced accuracy of 85.30%, macro-averaged F1 score of 82.34%, and a kappa coefficient of 0.83, while the RBF-SVM reached 81.19%, 83.06%, 77.68%, and 0.79, respectively. Solar panels, concrete, cobblestone, metallic materials, tree cover, and sparse grass showed high class-specific performance, whereas aged asphalt, bitumen roofing, and storage silos remained more difficult to distinguish. Overall, the results demonstrate the strong potential of airborne hyperspectral LWIR emissivity imaging for urban material discrimination under real-world conditions and support the development of dedicated LWIR spectral libraries for urban environments.

title: Monitoring Spatiotemporal Dynamics, Drivers, and Ecosystem Service Values of Small and Micro Wetlands in Anhui, China (1990–2020) Based on Multi-Temporal Landsat Data
summary: Comprehending the spatiotemporal dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and pattern-process relationships of small and micro wetlands (SMWs) holds paramount significance for their conservation, restoration, and sustainable management. We integrated Landsat imagery, land-use, topographic, climatic, socioeconomic, and statistical data for 1990–2020 in Anhui Province. Random forest classification, kernel density estimation, standard deviation ellipses, centroid migration, landscape metrics, land-use transition analysis, ecosystem service value (ESV) assessment, and Geodetector were used to characterize SMW change. Total SMW area increased from 53,843.67 ha in 1990 to 71,637.39 ha in 2020, while patch number increased from 104,011 to 125,971; patches smaller than 3 hm2 remained dominant. High-density areas were concentrated in the Jianghuai Plain, Yangtze River plain, Chaohu Lake region, and agricultural drainage networks, with a persistent northeast–southwest distribution orientation. Land-use transitions were dominated by exchanges among cropland, water bodies, and SMWs. At constant 2020 grain prices, total ESV increased from approximately CNY 3.668 billion in 1990 to CNY 6.840 billion in 2020, with hydrological regulation remaining among the largest service components. Geodetector results showed temporally varying single-factor spatial associations, while interaction patterns suggested potential joint spatial associations among natural and anthropogenic factors. These results support spatially targeted SMW conservation and management in Anhui Province.

title: Support-Aware Dual-SWIR Downscaling from Sentinel-2 and Submetre Jilin-1 Imagery on Non-Nested Grids
summary: Fine-scale shortwave-infrared (SWIR) imagery can support detailed land-surface mapping, but submetre satellites generally acquire only blue, green, red and near-infrared (RGBN) bands. Combining these data with Sentinel-2 SWIR requires an observation model that accounts for non-nested pixel supports. We developed a support-aware inverse-allocation framework using an RGBN-conditioned prior, exact polygon-overlap weights and a continuous correction field. The framework was evaluated in four regions of Xinjiang, China, using retained 20 m B11/B12 observations as reference. In a strictly matched control, replacing centre ownership with exact area overlap reduced mean joint root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 0.00174–0.00217 in reflectance units. The reduction occurred in all 15 non-nested phases and all 16 spatial blocks of each region. Continuous correction provided a further reduction of 0.000066–0.000166. Under a matched single-observation budget, the method achieved lower mean joint RMSE than adapted area-to-point regression kriging and DSen2 baselines in all four regions. Exact area overlap retained its advantage under controlled blur, ±10 m guide-image offsets and scale ratios of 2, 3 and 6, although the advantage narrowed at the coarsest ratio. Full-scene application to 0.75 m Jilin-1 RGBN and 20 m Sentinel-2 SWIR produced observation-consistent conditional SWIR allocations, with accuracy evaluated at the controlled 20 m reference resolution.

title: SARE-CD: Structure–Appearance Routed Experts for Building Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: In building change detection from high-resolution remote sensing imagery, genuine building changes typically appear as local alterations in roof contours and spatial layouts, whereas differences in solar elevation, atmospheric conditions, and sensor calibration introduce cross-temporal appearance drift in unchanged regions. When the two types of difference are jointly encoded in a single feature space, appearance drift tends to dominate the network response. We therefore propose SARE-CD, a dense, pixel-wise, soft-gated heterogeneous mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework that combines scene-level bias correction with functionally distinct expert modeling. At the feature front end, SARE-CD generates affine parameters from the channel statistics of the bitemporal change representation and applies them in residual form to suppress systematic radiometric drift. The Structure, Appearance, and Adaptive Experts then model geometric boundary changes, local appearance perturbations, and composite differences, respectively, and a pixel-wise router assigns expert weights at each location, with routing-entropy and weak load-balancing regularization used to stabilize the division of labor among the experts. On LEVIR-CD+, S2Looking, and SYSU-CD, SARE-CD achieves F1 scores of 91.58%, 65.78%, and 84.46%, all of which are the highest among the compared methods. In addition, controlled perturbation experiments show that F1 retention remains high under hue shifts, soft shadows, and small misregistration, whereas extreme additive brightness offsets lead to a notable F1 decline on S2Looking.

title: Counterfactual False-Positive Mining for Appearance-Robust Change Detection
summary: Appearance differences between acquisition dates can increase change responses at unchanged locations. Standard supervision on augmented pairs does not explicitly isolate this additional response. We define an input-level counterfactual response as the logit difference produced by the same fixed EMA teacher at the same pixel when the original time-2 image is replaced by a specified appearance intervention. This paired model response holds the scene geometry, label, teacher parameters, and operator realization fixed; it is not a causal reconstruction of the physical acquisition process. We propose counterfactual false-positive mining with reference prediction preservation (CFPM-RP). An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher compares an original pair with a pair undergoing a controlled appearance transformation. Positive logit increments within stable unchanged regions define candidate locations. A smooth one-sided loss penalizes the perturbed student response relative to the original teacher prediction, with auxiliary support weighting, segmentation supervision, and changed-region constraints. The auxiliary paths are used only during training, retaining the deployed detector architecture. Experiments cover LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD, eight appearance perturbations, an equal-budget continuation, eight additional comparison methods, and a second backbone. CFPM-RP attains perturbation-averaged F1 values of 91.444%, 71.181%, and 77.842% on the three datasets, respectively. Relative to Generic-FT, false-positive counts decrease by 10.37%, 11.15%, and 11.27%. The results show that CFPM-RP reduces appearance-induced false positives while retaining competitive change-detection performance.

title: Geo-Referenced Mobile RGB-D Sensing for Bicycle Lane Width Assessment
summary: Urban bicycle infrastructure requires spatially continuous and quantitative methods for assessing lane width under real operating conditions. This study presents a geo-referenced mobile RGB-D sensing framework for automated bicycle lane width measurement using a lightweight three-wheeled survey platform equipped with a stereo depth camera, GPS receiver, and inertial measurement unit. Bicycle lane boundaries are detected using FastSAM-based segmentation, GPU-accelerated Canny edge detection, and the Hough transform. IMU-assisted depth-to-height conversion distinguishes the road surface from curbs, roadside structures, and obstacles, while temporal-continuity-based lane restoration compensates for faded markings and occlusions. Lane width is estimated from three-dimensional Euclidean distances derived from RGB-D data. The measurements are temporally synchronized with GPS observations and mapped in a geographic information system to visualize spatial width variations along survey routes. Field experiments over four sections totaling 2.87 km showed that 97.79% of the width estimates were within ±5% of the reference width, with a mean absolute error of 0.0218 m. The resulting geo-referenced width maps enable spatially explicit identification of narrow or irregular bicycle lane sections for infrastructure inspection and maintenance.

title: Infrared UAV Target Recognition of PTZ Camera Based on Hybrid Action Space Reinforcement Learning
summary: With the rapid expansion of UAV applications, UAVs have posed growing challenges to public safety and airspace management. Pan–tilt–zoom (PTZ) cameras are widely used for monitoring, but conventional rule-based control lacks adaptability in dynamic environments, and existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods mostly rely on discrete action spaces with fixed time steps, preventing fine-grained camera adjustment. Meanwhile, infrared UAVs are often small, distant, and low-resolution, leading to low detection confidence and difficult classification. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hybrid-action-space DRL framework for PTZ camera control. PTZ control is modeled as a discrete-continuous hierarchical subspace: the agent selects a discrete action type and predicts its continuous execution duration for adaptive precise control. A target stable tracking reward function integrating object recognition accuracy, position, and size guides the agent to improve detection confidence and complete recognition efficiently. Furthermore, a lightweight multi-scale feature fusion recognition network combining CNN and Transformer is designed for accurate state representation, and two infrared UAV datasets are constructed to support training and evaluation. Experiments in a Unity3D-based simulation environment show that the proposed framework significantly improves detection confidence and recognition accuracy, maintains high tracking stability across multiple scenarios, and generalizes well with different object detectors, outperforming rule-based and single-action-space baselines.

title: Distinguishing Auroral-E and Sporadic-E in GNSS Radio Occultation Measurements
summary: GNSS radio occultation (RO) is widely used to detect metallic-ion sporadic-E layers on a global scale, but in auroral environments, particle precipitation-driven ionization can produce auroral-E structures with similar RO signatures. This overlap complicates reliable identification of sporadic-E and may bias high-latitude occurrence rate estimates. In this study, we quantify auroral contamination in RO-based sporadic-E detection and evaluate the performance of both threshold-based and multivariate classifier approaches. A dataset of 106 conjunction events was constructed using RO observations from the Spire and COSMIC-1 constellations, together with co-located ionosonde and magnetometer measurements at two high-latitude sites and an ionosonde at a mid-latitude site. Events were labeled as sporadic-E, auroral-E, or non-event from manual ionogram inspection. Two commonly used RO detection methods were applied: an excess phase perturbation Δϕ approach and an amplitude-based S4 approach. Results show that true sporadic-E events are primarily identified when both amplitude- and phase-based thresholds are satisfied. In contrast, more than 80% of auroral-E events satisfy at least one sporadic-E detection criterion, with false triggering of auroral-E and non-events dominated by the phase-based method. A Random Forest classifier was developed as a proof-of-concept model showing success at classifying sporadic-E and non-events, although ambiguity between auroral-E and sporadic-E persists likely due to overlapping phase-perturbation distributions. A Multiple Phase Screen Model is implemented to provide physical insight into the RO observations, where the vertically thicker auroral-E layers are shown to produce significant phase perturbations but negligible amplitude scintillation. These results demonstrate that RO-based detection methods identify E-region structure rather than formation mechanism, implying that high-latitude sporadic-E occurrence rates derived from phased-based RO observations are likely overestimated without additional context.

title: DARES: Rényi-Entropy Domain Adaptation for Forest Deforestation Segmentation
summary: Semantic segmentation of multispectral satellite imagery is central to large-scale tropical deforestation monitoring, yet cross-region deployment suffers from severe accuracy degradation due to radiometric, atmospheric, and geographic covariate shifts. We introduce dares (Domain Adaptation via Rényi Entropy for Semantic Segmentation), an unsupervised domain adaptation framework that transfers deforestation-mapping models across biomes without target annotations for training. Its core mechanism performs class-conditional Rényi-2 (α=2) alignment on the deepest feature grid together with decoupled confidence-weighted Rényi-2 entropy minimization on target predictions, stabilized against a degenerate collapse as detailed in Methods. Evaluated on an ecologically critical transfer task from the Brazilian Amazon to the Colombian deforestation arc using Sentinel-2 MSI data, dares attains 64.65% target-test mIoU (78.43% DICE) under moderate radiometric attenuation, numerically outperforming Source-Only (44.24%), ADVENT (50.24%), and CBST (48.92%) while maintaining 76.75% source-domain discriminability. Across a Low→Medium→High stress trajectory, dares follows a non-monotonic path from 75.42%→64.65%→69.54%, a 5.9-point Low-to-High change with a Medium dip and a High rebound. It is not the best at Low, where ADVENT (85.78%) and Source-Only (78.93%) exceed its 75.42%, while its advantage opens from Medium (+14.4 points over ADVENT, +20.4 over Source-Only) at the cost of the lowest source-test mIoU (76.75%). Component analysis indicates that decoupled entropy minimization drives target adaptation (−17.2 points if removed), whereas alignment, anti-collapse floors, and repulsion act as source-stabilizing regularizers rather than target maximizers.

title: Medicinal Plant Mapping Based on UAV Hyperspectral Imagery via an Interpretable Framework
summary: Accurate mapping of medicinal plants is essential for resource inventory and sustainable management. While Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) hyperspectral sensing provides a powerful monitoring tool, the high-dimensional spectral ambiguities and the black-box nature of conventional global classifiers severely restrict mapping accuracy and interpretability. To overcome this, we developed an interpretable, class-specific framework for fine-scale crop identification. A multi-feature pool was distilled through a hierarchical Successive Projections Algorithm (SPA)–Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS)–Genetic Algorithm (GA)–Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) strategy, isolating class-specific diagnostic fingerprints that transition mapping from black-box modeling to an explainable mechanism. The tailored feature subsets were supplied to parallel Random Forest binary classifiers to generate class-specific probability outputs, which were subsequently fed into a Logistic Regression decision-level fusion layer that calibrated prediction probabilities and resolved inter-class conflicts to yield the definitive classification results. Applied in Yunfu, Guangdong, the framework mapped target species (Murraya exotica, Zanthoxylum nitidum, and Melicope pteleifolia) with an overall accuracy of 97.35% (Kappa = 0.97), outperforming conventional benchmark models such as standard multi-class Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and spectral angle mapper. These findings demonstrate that coupling class-specific feature distillation with probability-calibrated decision fusion provides a robust, interpretable paradigm for precision agricultural mapping in heterogeneous environments.

title: Fine-Scale River-Ice-Type Mapping During the Freeze-Up Period Using UAV Multispectral Imagery
summary: The spatial distribution of river ice types during the freeze-up period provides important information on channel freezing and ice-cover development and serves as a basis for ice-condition monitoring and ice-jam flood risk assessment. However, river ice types differ considerably in spatial scale, spectral response, and surface structure, making their fine-scale identification under complex ice conditions challenging. In this study, nine representative frozen reaches along the Inner Mongolia section of the Yellow River were investigated using UAV multispectral orthomosaics with a spatial resolution of approximately 0.15 m. Four representative river-surface classes—open water, transparent ice, smooth ice, and rough ice—were mapped. Their responses in the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared bands were analyzed together with spectral indices and gray-level cooccurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features to characterize interclass spectral and textural differences. A deep-learning mapping model integrating multispectral and textural information was subsequently developed and evaluated on spatially independent reaches. Permutation importance was also used to quantify the contribution of each remote-sensing feature. The results showed that the four surface classes exhibited distinct spectral and textural characteristics. Transparent ice and open water showed limited spectral differences in several bands, whereas texture features captured differences in their local spatial structures and improved the model’s ability to distinguish spectrally similar classes. The model combining spectral indices and GLCM texture features accurately delineated the spatial distributions of the river ice types. In the spatially independent test reaches, it achieved an overall accuracy of 95.80%, a Macro-F1 score of 94.53%, and a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 90.14%. The model achieved an mIoU of 84.55% on an additional independent test reach with complex ice conditions, which was excluded from training and parameter optimization. Feature-contribution analysis identified spectral indices and texture features as important sources of discriminatory information. NDUWI and NDFSI, together with texture measures calculated from the red and near-infrared bands, ranked among the most informative inputs. This result suggests that the four river-surface classes were distinguished not only by their spectral differences but also by variations in local surface patterns. The UAV imagery therefore supported detailed mapping of heterogeneous frozen reaches and provided spatially explicit information relevant to ice-condition monitoring, analysis of river-ice development, and assessment of potential ice-jam flooding.

title: Passive microwave sea ice concentration biases in the Southern Hemisphere revealed by ICESat-2 linear ice fraction
summary: Gridded sea ice concentration (SIC) data are fundamental for understanding long-term polar climate. Since 1978, daily SIC data have been derived from passive microwave (PM) satellite observations. As SIC is not directly observed, it is obtained through an algorithmic inversion of PM brightness temperatures. Differences between PM-SIC algorithms lead to uncertainty in SIC data. Here we examine differences between several PM-SIC products and focus primarily on two: the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) Climate Data Record (CDR), which over our study period is derived from Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) data, and over the Southern Ocean is largely based on the Bootstrap (BT) PM-SIC algorithm, and the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2)-based NASATeam2 (NT2) product. On individual days, changes in integrated Antarctic sea ice area (SIA) can reach as high as 1.6 million km 2 in summer with relative differences up to 37% at the annual sea ice minimum. Using more than 1.8 million coincident observations of the ICESat-2 Linear Ice Fraction (LIF) from 2018 to 2024, we find BT-based PM-SIC data underestimate Antarctic SIC by a median of 0.2 in areas classified as the marginal ice zone (MIZ), corresponding to a median relative difference in SIC of 31%. This offset is seasonally, spatially, and parametrically consistent and yields differences in apparent MIZ extent as high as 4.4 million km 2 . The offset exceeds reported CDR uncertainties that average 0.07 and cannot be explained as a consequence of sensor differences. The parametric simplicity of the observed bias means these offsets can be parameterized as a function of BT SIC alone, which could lead to an improved SIC dataset for Antarctic studies.

title: A revised model for atmospheric adjacency effect correction in optical satellite earth observation images
